images.title: Move left from 85
images.purpose: Show that 85 + (−60) is found on an unmarked number line by starting at 85 and moving 60 to the left, landing on 25.
images.composition: One long horizontal line across the middle with only three marks, a long arrow above it, and one equation centred below.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal line in grey #6B7280 with arrowheads at both ends and exactly 3 tick marks placed to scale: 0 at the left, 25 at 25 units from 0, and 85 at 85 units from 0. The 85 mark is teal #0072B2, the 25 mark is amber #E69F00, the 0 mark is plain. One long arrow in reddish purple #CC79A7 above the line from 85 back to 25, pointing left, labelled 60 left. No other ticks. Exactly 3 marks, 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
extra tick marks or numbers on the line other than the three listed
images.takeaway: Adding a negative number moves you to the left.
images.description: An unmarked line with only 0, 25 and 85, and a leftward arrow of 60 from 85 to 25 under the equation 85 + (−60) = 25.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say which way the arrow points and why adding a negative goes left.

image_decisions.why: Drawing only the needed marks on an unmarked line is a picture idea; one clean line carries it.
